checks.desc: The number of pages indexed by Google/Bing and other search engines and the number of pages in the site structure is consistent
checks.observation:
Screaming Frog : 17 768 crawled URL / 17 722 crawled indexable URL (without Javascript) Screaming Frog : warning => more than 110 636 crawled URL / 19 553 crawled indexable URL (with Javascript)
 Google Search Console : 11 844 indexed URL (-33%) Bing Webmaster Tool : 31,5K indexed URL (+78%)

 Issue 1 - Google under-indexation (−5,878 URLs)
 2 likely causes:

 Crawled – currently not indexed: Google crawled the pages but judged their value insufficient to index (thin content or excessive similarity with other pages).
 Discovered – currently not indexed: URLs known via sitemap/internal linking, but not visited due to unallocated crawl budget.

 Issue 2 - Bing over-indexation (+13,778 URLs)
 1 most likely cause:

 Bing doesn't respect your robots.txt file, in fact.

 Observation: The robots.txt correctly blocks 3 Magento applicative modules, but internal links expose them to crawlers regardless - generating 57 945 blocked URLs, representing 74.3% of the total crawl (77 943 URLs). The 3 patterns account for 96.6% of blocked URLs: /anpconfigurator (41.7%), /customer (36.6%), /weareplanet_payment (18.3%). /customer is the critical leak - confirmed present in static HTML (12,596 URLs in no-JS crawl), meaning Googlebot discovers it without rendering. The other 2 are JS-generated only. GSC reports 15,987 URLs blocked on Google's side.

 Solution : Remove functional URLs from crawlable HTML links across the site. 3 distinct patterns identified during the audit, each requiring a tailored fix:

 1. /customer/account/login and /customer/account/create
 Currently exposed as static <a href> links in the site header on all pages. Replace with <button> elements triggering a modal or client-side navigation. The routes remain functional for authenticated actions but are no longer exposed in the DOM, removing them from the crawlable surface sitewide.

 Recommended fix: <button> or <input>

 2. /anpconfigurator/article_dimensions/... (product pages with dimensional configuration)

 Example:

 https://www.apsoparts.com/de-CH/10250806-einsteckprofil-mit-hohlraum.html

 https://www.apsoparts.com/de-CH/anpconfigurator/article_dimensions/index/productSku/10250806/articleSku/1025088921/ (internal link on product page)

 Currently exposed as static <a href> links on product pages with dimensional configuration (cut-to-length products: profiles, cords, belts, foam profiles, etc.).

 Each productSku × articleSku combination generates a distinct crawlable URL, likely producing thousands of parasitic URLs across the catalog with zero SEO/GEO value. A Disallow: */anpconfigurator/ rule currently exists in robots.txt, which prevents Googlebot from requesting these URLs but does not remove them from Google's discovery graph.

 Recommended fix: replace with JS-triggered configurator opening (client-side state, no URL exposed in DOM). The Disallow rule becomes redundant and can be removed afterward.

 3. /weareplanet_payment/checkout/deviceSession/ (payment fingerprinting... apparently)

 Example:

 https://www.apsoparts.com/nl-NL/16800223-rsp-150.html

 https://www.apsoparts.com/nl-NL/weareplanet_payment/checkout/deviceSession/?_=1782400717040 (internal link on product page too)

 Different pattern. This endpoint is not exposed as <a href> but invoked via runtime JavaScript XHR by the WeArePlanet Payment module, which loads on every page load sitewide, not only at checkout. A Disallow: */weareplanet_payment* rule is in place and confirmed functional (Screaming Frog crawl in "Respect robots.txt" mode reports these URLs as Blocked by Robots.txt). However, the URLs remain discoverable through the XHR call detected at JS rendering, and the script contributes to the elevated JavaScript execution time observed in the webperf audit (5.4s JS on product pages).

 Recommended fix: scope the WeArePlanet script to checkout and cart pages only, via a conditional module trigger in Magento.

 The remaining checkpoints of the technical audit will allow us to refine and complete this analysis - in particular by cross-referencing canonical management, internal linking patterns, sitemap accuracy, and the granular handling of URL parameters across both search engines.

checks.observation:
Observation:
 Rel="prev/next" are not set up in order for search engines to understand the relation between paginated contents. Page checked = https://www.apsoparts.com/fr-FR/technologie-de-l-etancheite/joints-toriques-x-rings.html?p=2 Reality is that this point is useless for Google since 2019, and no specific guidelines on this topic for LLM. However, it is still important for Bing and Yandex.

 Solution :
 Please find below the good practices for pagination:
 => In the case of a sequence of pages, pagination allows robots to know the relationship between pages and makes it easier for users to navigate.
 - use <link> tags rel = "prev" and rel = "next" to indicate relationships between pages
 - paginated pages can be tracked by indexing robots: make sure you don't set a nofollow attribute
 - each page in the paginated series must have a canonical tag pointing to itself or to the "view-all" page
 - the link pointing to page 1 of the series must be correct and not domain/p=1 or domain/page=1
 - the 1st page of the paginated series must not contain a rel = "prev" tag (there is only one rel="next" link tag on the first page)
 - the last page of the paginated series must not contain a rel = "next" tag (there is only one rel="prev" link tag on the last page)
 - paginated series must follow a logical sequence (e.g. page 3 must have a rel = "prev" to page 2 and a rel = "next" to page 4).
 - pagination links must be in HTML and not in JavaScript (especially in the case of infinite scrolling)

Observation:
 On your product pages, several elements with high GEO value are invisible to LLM bots because they are injected via JavaScript:

 The content must be rendered as static HTML server-side at initial page load, with JavaScript interactivity (filters, sorting, dynamic anchors) layered on top as progressive enhancement - meaning it adds to an already complete HTML base rather than replacing it. Magento supports this natively through standard PHP blocks instead of Knockout.js components. This is a structural IT project to scope with your technical team, and should be prioritized as chantier #1 of the GEO roadmap, as it gates LLM citation across the entire product catalog.

checks.desc: Hreflang tags are correctly implemented to target specific languages and regions
checks.observation:
Observation:
 The hreflang implementation on your product pages is technically well-structured (absolute HTTPS URLs, x-default declared, self-referencing valid), but contains 3 significant inconsistencies:

 (1) Missing de-DE and de-AT hreflang - Magento stores exist for Germany (germany_eur_de) and Austria (austria_eur_de) and are exposed in your country switcher, but no hreflang declares them. German users on Google.de may be routed to your de-CH version with Swiss currency (CHF) and logistics, instead of the German store. Likely the most consequential gap given the size of the German industrial market for your business.
 (2) Missing en-FR and en-CH hreflang - Your language switcher exposes an English store for France (france_eur_en) and Switzerland, but no regional English hreflang is declared. The x-default pointing to /en-INT/ serves as a catch-all, but English speakers in France or Switzerland are not directed to their regional English store.
 (3) Inconsistent slug localization across markets - Only Polish has a fully localized URL slug (pierscien-x-nbr-70-315-04). All other non-English markets (FR, IT, NL, DE) use the English slug x-ring-nbr-70-315-04. This weakens both SEO (lower keyword match in local searches) and GEO (LLMs rely heavily on URL semantics for content identification).

 Solution :
 A 3-step remediation plan:

 (1) Add the missing hreflang variants - Priority on de-DE and de-AT (business-critical for the German-speaking industrial market), followed by en-FR and en-CH if your regional English stores are actively used. This is a template-level fix in Magento, applicable sitewide.
 (2) Decide a single policy on URL slug localization and apply it sitewide - Either fully localize slugs across all non-English markets (recommended for SEO and GEO impact, aligning with your current Polish approach) or harmonize on English-only slugs. The current mixed approach is the worst of both worlds.
 (3) After...Audit hreflang reciprocity via Screaming Frog - Run the Hreflang report on a representative sample of product pages across all locales to confirm bidirectional consistency. Any non-reciprocal declaration is silently ignored by Google and must be corrected. An other specific technical topic (point number 3) to lead => Annual SEO run management.

The number of key requests counts low and transfer size is small.
checks.observation:
Observation:
 The "Network dependency tree" audit is explicitly listed as failed across all 4 templates (Home, L1, L2, Product page). This confirms an excessive number of key requests and/or large transfer sizes in the critical request chain. Total network weight further supports this - Home is the most severe at 6 922 Kio, with L2 at 2 428 Kio, L1 at 2 134 Kio, and Product page at 1 859 Kio.

 Solution :
 Reduce the number of critical requests by inlining small CSS/JS, combining assets where possible, and deferring non-critical resources. Minimize transfer sizes by applying compression, next-gen image formats, and removing unused CSS/JS. Preloading key resources with <link rel="preload"> will also shorten the critical path length.
checks.found: Too many and too heavy key requests.
checks.ask: Fewer and smaller critical requests: inline small files, compress, preload.

checks.desc: Chaining critical requests (sequences of essential requests for page rendering that depend on one another) are avoided
checks.observation:
Observation:
 The "Network dependency tree" audit is explicitly listed as failed across all 4 templates (Home, L1, L2, Product page). Chained critical requests are a confirmed issue sitewide, directly contributing to the severe Lab LCP scores - Homepage: 29.7s, L1: 16.1s, L2: 17.1s, Product page: 10.6s - and the render-blocking penalties ranging from -1 660ms to -2 980ms across templates.

 Solution :
 Flatten the critical request chain by inlining critical CSS directly in the <head>, preloading key resources with <link rel="preload">, and eliminating render-blocking dependencies between CSS and JS. Ensure the LCP image is discoverable in the initial HTML response without requiring intermediate requests to resolve first.
checks.found: Critical requests are chained.
checks.ask: Shorten the chain of critical requests: inline critical CSS, preload key files.
